
**Only specs contain rules. A plan covers rules and contains none.** A `covers` entry is a rule ref (`WL-RULE-<n>`), a `<doc>#sec-N` entry, which resolves to the rule at that anchor and the rules arranged under it, or a whole-document entry, which resolves to every rule the document contains. Entries are resolved when the plan is written, and each resolved rule is stored as a `covers` edge from the plan to the rule. An entry whose target has no rules yet is stored unresolved in `to_external`; a later write that mints that document's rules resolves it, and `lode doc resolve` (admin, `POST /api/v1/docs/covers/resolve`) re-resolves every entry still stranded. A plan has no `doc_rules` rows, and its prose mints no rule. Governing rules at mint and at plan close (WL-REQ-1356), plan staleness on withdrawal (WL-SPEC-77#sec-9h) and which plans cover a rule all read these edges, and the rule detail lists the covering plans. Coverage follows supersession: a successor counts as covered when its predecessors were.

**A `covers` edge means the plan builds the whole requirement.** There are no coverage levels, and only requirements are covered. A section or whole-document entry resolves to the requirements and catalogues in its scope and skips invariants, definitions and principles; a direct ref to a rule of another kind is refused. A plan's covered set is the union of the requirements its entries resolve to, and nested entries (`WL-SPEC-77#sec-4` and `WL-SPEC-77#sec-4a`) simply overlap. A requirement two plans each build part of is too big: split it (WL-SPEC-77#sec-4n) so each plan covers whole requirements.
